# Power-and-Propulsion Availability Supervisor

## Selected system context

### Synopsis

NEED-01: A single forest-fire observation drone has a selected battery, power-management
equipment, a charger, and an explicit four-engine configuration, but the seed provides
no policy for deciding whether a propulsion-power enable command may be issued from
qualitative equipment evidence.

PURPOSE-01: The system shall obtain and analyze a finite qualitative battery
observation, assess selected power, charging, engine-group, and configuration evidence,
manage a drone-control enable demand, and issue only a fail-closed propulsion-power
command and an explanatory availability report.

### Evidence and claim classes

ASM-01: The surrounding integration environment, represented by CTX-01 through CTX-05,
is responsible for presenting one complete finite input snapshot per discrete logical
evaluation. Logical evaluations support deterministic model analysis and make no
physical timing, scheduling, or latency claim.

ASM-02: CTX-02 through CTX-04 are responsible for the declared validity and freshness
tags. `VALID` and `CURRENT` mean only admitted by this pilot policy; they do not
establish measurement truth or hardware performance.

ASM-03: CTX-01 is responsible for issuing exactly one `ControlEvent` value per
evaluation. Event mutual exclusion is a selected interface convention because the seed
defines no human actor or control protocol.

ASM-04: CTX-05 is responsible for reporting one `ActuationFeedback` value per
evaluation. `ENABLED_CONFIRMED` and `DISABLED_CONFIRMED` are abstract acknowledgments,
not proof that engines generate thrust or that physical power changed.

ASM-05: The finite evidence alphabets and exact acceptance, priority, initialization,
and recovery rules below are Designer-selected abstractions needed for exhaustive
analysis; none is a source-defined hardware policy.

ASM-06: Missing or unusable information is represented by `UNKNOWN`, `UNAVAILABLE`,
`INVALID`, or `STALE`, as applicable, rather than by an absent interaction. This closes
the finite boundary partitions without prescribing transport.

ASM-07: CTX-01 must interpret `AVAILABLE_FOR_ENABLE` and every enable command only as
results of this abstract policy and must not treat them as observation permission,
mission authority, safety approval, or physical performance assurance.

### Goals

GOAL-01: The system shall initialize and fail closed: an unqualified battery
observation, any rejected power/propulsion/charging evidence, an active fault, a closed
recovery gate, no active demand, an accepted disable or recovery event, or an
unconfirmed initial state shall prevent `ENABLE_NEW` and `ENABLE_HOLD`. Pass criterion:
bounded analysis finds no counterexample over the complete admitted partitions.

GOAL-02: The system shall issue an enable command only after a fresh post-recovery
enable request, admitted evidence from every assessment owner, an open recovery gate,
and a fault-free priority result. Pass criterion: the system composition relation is
equivalent to that conjunction on every producer-reachable valuation.

GOAL-03: The system shall deterministically expose one limiting cause using the fixed
cause and action priorities. Pass criterion: every unavailable producer-reachable
valuation has exactly one cause and no available valuation has a non-`NONE` cause.

GOAL-04: The system shall distribute retained state across demand, recovery, and
command-interlock owners and distribute current decisions across the ten other owners.
Pass criterion: owner-local contracts and analyzer results demonstrate a nonidentity
derivation for every PART-01 through PART-13.

GOAL-05: A fault shall invalidate the pre-fault demand; fault clearance and
acknowledgment shall reopen recovery but shall not restore enablement until CTX-01
issues a new request. Pass criterion: all recovery scenarios show `DISABLE` from the
initiating fault through acknowledgment and until a fresh request completes the
request-to-command pipeline.

### Operational context and exact boundary

CTX-01: The drone-control client is outside the system. It supplies enable, disable, and
recovery-acknowledgment events and receives the availability report. This contextual
role is inferred from the seed's drone-control equipment and battery-status flow.

CTX-02: The battery and power-status source is outside the system. It supplies the
qualitative battery observation and power-management evidence; the system neither
measures electrochemical state nor controls charging physics.

CTX-03: The engine and configuration evidence source is outside the system. It supplies
two engine-group snapshots and a structural configuration snapshot without asserting
their truth or any flight consequence.

CTX-04: The charging context source is outside the system. It reports whether the named
charger is disconnected, connected idle, charging, or unknown; charging control remains
external.

CTX-05: The power-and-propulsion actuation recipient is outside the system. It receives
the abstract power command and supplies acknowledgment feedback; downstream electrical
switching and engine actuation are not modeled.

CTX-06: The forest-fire environment provides domain context only and has no direct
modeled interaction. No fire property, observation state, or sortie state organizes this
system's policy.

MON-01: `batteryObservation`, supplied by CTX-02, has type `BatteryObservation =
{quality: ADEQUATE | LIMITED | DEPLETED | UNKNOWN, validity: VALID | INVALID, freshness:
CURRENT | STALE}`. The four quality values are a downstream finite abstraction of the
seed's unenumerated qualitative status.

MON-02: `powerManagementEvidence`, supplied by CTX-02, has type `PowerEvidence =
{condition: NOMINAL | DEGRADED | UNAVAILABLE | UNKNOWN, validity: VALID | INVALID,
freshness: CURRENT | STALE}`.

MON-03: `oddEngineGroupEvidence`, supplied by CTX-03, has type `EnginePairEvidence =
{first, second: NOMINAL | NON_NOMINAL | UNAVAILABLE | UNKNOWN, validity: VALID |
INVALID, freshness: CURRENT | STALE}` and represents engines 1 and 3 only as distinct
named positions.

MON-04: `evenEngineGroupEvidence`, supplied by CTX-03, has the same `EnginePairEvidence`
type and represents engines 2 and 4 only as distinct named positions.

MON-05: `configurationEvidence`, supplied by CTX-03, has type `ConfigurationEvidence =
{engineCount: FOUR | OTHER | UNKNOWN, alternatingKinds: MATCHES_SOURCE | DOES_NOT_MATCH
| UNKNOWN, validity: VALID | INVALID, freshness: CURRENT | STALE}`. `MATCHES_SOURCE`
means structural concordance only.

MON-06: `chargerEvidence`, supplied by CTX-04, has type `ChargerEvidence = {coupling:
DISCONNECTED | CONNECTED_IDLE | CHARGING | UNKNOWN, validity: VALID | INVALID,
freshness: CURRENT | STALE}`.

MON-07: `controlEvent`, supplied by CTX-01, has type `ControlEvent = NONE |
REQUEST_ENABLE | REQUEST_DISABLE | ACKNOWLEDGE_RECOVERY`.

MON-08: `actuationFeedback`, supplied by CTX-05, has type `ActuationFeedback =
DISABLED_CONFIRMED | ENABLED_CONFIRMED | UNKNOWN` and contains no physical-performance
claim.

CTRL-01: `propulsionPowerCommand`, received by CTX-05, has type `PowerCommand = DISABLE
| ENABLE_NEW | ENABLE_HOLD`. `ENABLE_NEW` marks the first enable command of one admitted
demand; `ENABLE_HOLD` maintains that admitted demand without creating another fresh
command cycle.

CTRL-02: `availabilityReport`, received by CTX-01, has type `AvailabilityReport =
{decision: UNAVAILABLE | AVAILABLE_FOR_ENABLE, cause: NONE | BATTERY | POWER_MANAGEMENT
| ODD_ENGINE_GROUP | EVEN_ENGINE_GROUP | CONFIGURATION | CHARGER | RECOVERY | NO_DEMAND
| OPERATOR_DISABLE, demand: IDLE | REQUESTED | ACTIVE, recovery: NORMAL | QUARANTINED |
AWAITING_ACK}`. Copied demand/recovery fields are observable context but earn PART-12 no
owner credit.

### Risks, faults, degraded behavior, and recovery

RISK-01: If invalid, stale, limited, unavailable, non-nominal, structurally discordant,
connected-charger, or unknown evidence were admitted, an enable command could be issued
outside the selected policy. No likelihood or physical severity is asserted.

RISK-02: If fault clearance restored a pre-fault demand, the system could resume
enablement without a new drone-control request.

RISK-03: If retained availability or command state outranked a current disable, fault,
or recovery condition, the system could continue an enable command for one stale
evaluation.

RISK-04: Repeated enable events or delayed acknowledgments could create repeated
`ENABLE_NEW` commands for one continuous demand.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Gate the original model, then create an isolated executable/codegen projection.
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  echo "usage: $0 <agent/M-star.sysml> <new-work-directory> [external/sysml-aadl-libraries]" >&2
  exit 2
}

[[ $# -ge 2 && $# -le 3 ]] || usage

script_dir=$(realpath "$(dirname "$0")")
repo_root=$(realpath "$script_dir/..")
model=$(realpath "$1")
work_arg=$2
library=$(realpath "${3:-$repo_root/external/sysml-aadl-libraries}")

lower_model=${model,,}
case "/$lower_model/" in
  */evaluator/*|*/oracle.sysml/) echo "refusing evaluator/oracle model path" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
[[ -f $model && $model == *.sysml ]] || { echo "candidate model not found: $model" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ -d $library ]] || { echo "SysML AADL library not found: $library" >&2; exit 2; }
requirements="$(dirname "$model")/N.md"
[[ -f $requirements ]] || { echo "candidate requirements not found beside model: $requirements" >&2; exit 2; }

if [[ -e $work_arg ]]; then
  work=$(realpath "$work_arg")
  if find "$work" -mindepth 1 -print -quit | grep -q .; then
    echo "work directory must be new or empty: $work" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
else
  mkdir -p "$work_arg"
  work=$(realpath "$work_arg")
fi

if [[ -n ${SIREUM_BIN:-} ]]; then
  sireum=$(realpath "$SIREUM_BIN")
elif [[ -n ${SIREUM_HOME:-} ]]; then
  sireum=$(realpath "$SIREUM_HOME/bin/sireum")
else
  sireum=$(command -v sireum || true)
fi
[[ -n $sireum && -x $sireum ]] || {
  echo "Sireum executable not found; set SIREUM_BIN or SIREUM_HOME" >&2
  exit 2
}

mkdir -p "$work/evidence" "$work/staged" "$work/hamr"
cp "$requirements" "$work/N.md"
if [[ -f "$(dirname "$model")/.poolside/settings.local.yaml" ]]; then
  mkdir -p "$work/.poolside"
  cp "$(dirname "$model")/.poolside/settings.local.yaml" "$work/.poolside/settings.local.yaml"
fi
source_hash_before=$(sha256sum "$model" | awk '{print $1}')

# Acceptance gate 1 is intentionally run against the original candidate, not
# the executable projection. Keep the invocation identical to the campaign's
# named `sireum hamr sysml logika` gate.
set +e
"$sireum" hamr sysml logika \
  --sourcepath "$library" \
  "$model" >"$work/evidence/original-model-logika.log" 2>&1
integration_rc=$?
set -e
cat "$work/evidence/original-model-logika.log"
if [[ $integration_rc -ne 0 ]] || \
   grep -Eqi 'Resolution error:|Compilation failed|(^|[[:space:]])error:' "$work/evidence/original-model-logika.log"; then
  echo "ORIGINAL_MODEL_LOGIKA_FAILED rc=$integration_rc" >&2
  exit 1
fi

projection="$work/staged/M-star.executable.sysml"
metadata="$work/staged/projection.json"
python3 "$script_dir/stage_executable_model.py" \
  "$model" "$projection" "$metadata" >"$work/evidence/projection.jsonl"

package=$(python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["package"])' "$metadata")
system_name=$(python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["system_name"])' "$metadata")
slang_package=$(printf '%s' "$package" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')

set +e
"$sireum" hamr sysml codegen \
  --platform JVM \
  --runtime-monitoring \
  --package-name "$slang_package" \
  --output-dir "$work/hamr" \
  --slang-output-dir "$work/hamr/slang" \
  --no-proyek-ive \
  --workspace-root-dir "$work/staged" \
  --sourcepath "$work/staged:$library" \
  --system-name "$system_name" \
  "$projection" >"$work/evidence/codegen.log" 2>&1
codegen_rc=$?
set -e
cat "$work/evidence/codegen.log"
if [[ $codegen_rc -ne 0 ]] || grep -Eqi 'Resolution error:|Compilation failed|(^|[[:space:]])error:' "$work/evidence/codegen.log"; then
  echo "EXECUTABLE_CODEGEN_FAILED rc=$codegen_rc" >&2
  exit 1
fi

slang="$work/hamr/slang"
component_root="$slang/src/main/component"
[[ -f $slang/bin/project.cmd ]] || { echo "codegen produced no Proyek project" >&2; exit 1; }
mapfile -d '' components < <(find "$component_root" -type f -name '*.scala' -print0 | sort -z)
[[ ${#components[@]} -gt 0 ]] || { echo "codegen produced no component applications" >&2; exit 1; }
for component in "${components[@]}"; do
  grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*def[[:space:]]+initialise[[:space:]]*\(' "$component" || {
    echo "generated component lacks initialise: $component" >&2; exit 1;
  }
  grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*def[[:space:]]+timeTriggered[[:space:]]*\(' "$component" || {
    echo "generated component lacks timeTriggered: $component" >&2; exit 1;
  }
done

source_hash_after=$(sha256sum "$model" | awk '{print $1}')
[[ $source_hash_before == "$source_hash_after" ]] || {
  echo "original candidate changed during projection/codegen" >&2; exit 1;
}

# Freeze the generated surface outside HAMR's application files.  The later
# proof gate verifies both this hash manifest and the component-file allowlist.
(
  cd "$slang"
  find . -type f \
    ! -path './src/main/component/*' \
    ! -path './out/*' \
    -print0 \
    | sort -z \
    | xargs -0 sha256sum
) >"$work/generated-nonapplication.sha256"
(
  cd "$slang"
  find src/main/component -type f -name '*.scala' -print | sort
) >"$work/generated-component-files.txt"
cp "$script_dir/run-logika.sh" "$work/run-logika.sh"
chmod u+x "$work/run-logika.sh"

cat >"$work/APPLICATION_PHASE.txt" <<EOF
POOLside application phase boundary

Writable application files:
  $component_root/**/*.scala

Read-only requirements:
  $work/N.md

Do not edit the staged SysML, generated bridge/API/data/runtime/project files,
the manifests, or this gate.  After the application agent implements every
generated initialise and timeTriggered body, run the command below.  HAMR
Initialization_Api values expose output setters but no input getters: initialise
must establish safe state/outputs without reading an input port.

  $work/run-logika.sh $slang $work/proof
EOF

# Protect the entire retained phase input, while excluding Logika's mutable
# cache/output tree and the application allowlist itself.
(
  cd "$work"
  find . -type f \
    ! -path './hamr/slang/src/main/component/*' \
    ! -path './hamr/slang/out/*' \
    ! -path './proof/*' \
    ! -path './protected-work-files.sha256' \
    -print0 \
    | sort -z \
    | xargs -0 sha256sum
) >"$work/protected-work-files.sha256"
find "$work" -type f \
  ! -path "$component_root/*" \
  ! -path "$slang/out/*" \
  ! -path "$work/proof/*" \
  -exec chmod a-w {} +
find "$component_root" -type f -name '*.scala' -exec chmod u+w,go-w {} +

printf 'EXECUTABLE_PREPARED work=%s components=%s system=%s\n' \
  "$work" "${#components[@]}" "$system_name"
printf 'APPLICATION_ROOT=%s\n' "$component_root"
printf 'NEXT=%q\ %q\ %q\n' "$work/run-logika.sh" "$slang" "$work/proof"

def portable_path(path: Path) -> str:
    return Path(os.path.relpath(path.resolve(), Path.cwd().resolve())).as_posix()

    lowered = {part.lower() for part in path.parts}

def strip_gumbo_initialization_sections(text: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """Remove initialization contracts from the non-normative codegen view.

    HAMR initialization APIs do not expose input ports.  Consequently, an
    otherwise valid model-level ``initialize`` guarantee that refers to an
    input generates uncompilable Slang (both Initialization_Api and PostState
    containers lack that member).  Selectively rewriting expressions would
    invent semantics, so the executable projection consistently removes the
    complete initialization section from every GUMBO block.  The original
    candidate is checked by model Logika before this projection is created.

    Whitespace replacement preserves line numbers for diagnostics and leaves
    state, functions, invariants, integration, and compute sections verbatim.
    """
    removed = 0

    def project_block(block_match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
        nonlocal removed
        body = block_match.group("body")

        def remove_section(section_match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
            nonlocal removed
            removed += 1
            return _blank_preserving_lines(section_match.group(0))

        projected_body = GUMBO_INITIALIZE.sub(remove_section, body)
        return block_match.group("open") + projected_body + block_match.group("close")

    return GUMBO_BLOCK.sub(project_block, text), removed


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("source", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("destination", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("metadata", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--period-ms", type=int, default=1000)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    source = args.source.resolve()
    destination = args.destination.resolve()
    metadata = args.metadata.resolve()
    reject_contaminating_path(source)
    if args.period_ms <= 0:
        raise SystemExit("--period-ms must be positive")

    original = source.read_bytes()
    text = original.decode("utf-8")
    packages = PACKAGE.findall(text)
    if len(packages) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(f"expected exactly one package, found {packages}")
    system_defs = set(SYSTEM_DEF.findall(text))
    system_uses = [
        (len(match.group("indent").expandtabs()), match.group("target"))
        for match in PART_USE.finditer(text)
        if match.group("target") in system_defs
    ]
    shallowest = min((depth for depth, _ in system_uses), default=-1)
    roots = [target for depth, target in system_uses if depth == shallowest]
    if len(roots) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(
            "expected exactly one root part usage targeting a System definition, "
            f"found {roots}"
        )
    if re.search(r"\bDispatch_Protocol\b|attribute\s+:>>\s+Period\b", text):
        raise SystemExit(
            "candidate already contains dispatch/period refinements; refusing to "
            "guess how to normalize them"
        )

    count = 0

    def add_periodic(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
        nonlocal count
        count += 1
        indent = match.group("indent") + "  "
        return (
            match.group(0)
            + "\n"
            + indent
            + "attribute :>> Dispatch_Protocol = Periodic;\n"
            + indent
            + f"attribute :>> Period = {args.period_ms} [ms];"
        )

    projected = THREAD.sub(add_periodic, text)
    if count == 0:
        raise SystemExit("candidate contains no Thread definitions")
    if projected.count("attribute :>> Dispatch_Protocol = Periodic;") != count:
        raise SystemExit("internal projection error: dispatch count does not match Threads")
    if projected.count(f"attribute :>> Period = {args.period_ms} [ms];") != count:
        raise SystemExit("internal projection error: period count does not match Threads")
    periodic_projection = projected
    projected, initialization_sections_removed = strip_gumbo_initialization_sections(
        periodic_projection
    )
    if projected.count("\n") != periodic_projection.count("\n"):
        raise SystemExit("internal projection error: initialization removal changed line count")
    remaining_initialization_headers = sum(
        len(re.findall(r"(?m)^[ \t]*initialize[ \t]*$", match.group("body")))
        for match in GUMBO_BLOCK.finditer(projected)
    )
    if remaining_initialization_headers:
        raise SystemExit(
            "unsupported GUMBO initialization layout remained after codegen projection"
        )

    destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    metadata.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    destination.write_text(projected, encoding="utf-8")
    result = {
        "schema_version": 1,
        "source": portable_path(source),
        "source_sha256": sha256(original),
        "projection": portable_path(destination),
        "projection_sha256": sha256(projected.encode("utf-8")),
        "package": packages[0],
        "system_definition": roots[0],
        "system_name": f"{packages[0]}::{roots[0]}",
        "thread_count": count,
        "period_ms": args.period_ms,
        "initialization_projection": "removed_from_codegen_view",
        "initialization_sections_removed": initialization_sections_removed,
    }
    metadata.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps(result))
    return 0

  echo "protected application-phase inputs changed after preparation" >&2

  echo "component application file set differs from the generated allowlist" >&2
  diff -u "$allowlist" "$current" >&2 || true

process_timeout=${LOGIKA_PROCESS_TIMEOUT:-180}

      failures=$((failures + 1))

      echo "LOGIKA_PASSED component=$relative method=$method"
    fi
  done

  exit 1
fi

## Selected system context

### Synopsis

NEED-01: A single forest-fire observation drone has a selected battery, power-management
equipment, a charger, and an explicit four-engine configuration, but the seed provides
no policy for deciding whether a propulsion-power enable command may be issued from
qualitative equipment evidence.

PURPOSE-01: The system shall obtain and analyze a finite qualitative battery
observation, assess selected power, charging, engine-group, and configuration evidence,
manage a drone-control enable demand, and issue only a fail-closed propulsion-power
command and an explanatory availability report.

### Evidence and claim classes

ASM-01: The surrounding integration environment, represented by CTX-01 through CTX-05,
is responsible for presenting one complete finite input snapshot per discrete logical
evaluation. Logical evaluations support deterministic model analysis and make no
physical timing, scheduling, or latency claim.

ASM-02: CTX-02 through CTX-04 are responsible for the declared validity and freshness
tags. `VALID` and `CURRENT` mean only admitted by this pilot policy; they do not
establish measurement truth or hardware performance.

ASM-03: CTX-01 is responsible for issuing exactly one `ControlEvent` value per
evaluation. Event mutual exclusion is a selected interface convention because the seed
defines no human actor or control protocol.

ASM-04: CTX-05 is responsible for reporting one `ActuationFeedback` value per
evaluation. `ENABLED_CONFIRMED` and `DISABLED_CONFIRMED` are abstract acknowledgments,
not proof that engines generate thrust or that physical power changed.

ASM-05: The finite evidence alphabets and exact acceptance, priority, initialization,
and recovery rules below are Designer-selected abstractions needed for exhaustive
analysis; none is a source-defined hardware policy.

ASM-06: Missing or unusable information is represented by `UNKNOWN`, `UNAVAILABLE`,
`INVALID`, or `STALE`, as applicable, rather than by an absent interaction. This closes
the finite boundary partitions without prescribing transport.

ASM-07: CTX-01 must interpret `AVAILABLE_FOR_ENABLE` and every enable command only as
results of this abstract policy and must not treat them as observation permission,
mission authority, safety approval, or physical performance assurance.

### Goals

GOAL-01: The system shall initialize and fail closed: an unqualified battery
observation, any rejected power/propulsion/charging evidence, an active fault, a closed
recovery gate, no active demand, an accepted disable or recovery event, or an
unconfirmed initial state shall prevent `ENABLE_NEW` and `ENABLE_HOLD`. Pass criterion:
bounded analysis finds no counterexample over the complete admitted partitions.

GOAL-02: The system shall issue an enable command only after a fresh post-recovery
enable request, admitted evidence from every assessment owner, an open recovery gate,
and a fault-free priority result. Pass criterion: the system composition relation is
equivalent to that conjunction on every producer-reachable valuation.

GOAL-03: The system shall deterministically expose one limiting cause using the fixed
cause and action priorities. Pass criterion: every unavailable producer-reachable
valuation has exactly one cause and no available valuation has a non-`NONE` cause.

GOAL-04: The system shall distribute retained state across demand, recovery, and
command-interlock owners and distribute current decisions across the ten other owners.
Pass criterion: owner-local contracts and analyzer results demonstrate a nonidentity
derivation for every PART-01 through PART-13.

GOAL-05: A fault shall invalidate the pre-fault demand; fault clearance and
acknowledgment shall reopen recovery but shall not restore enablement until CTX-01
issues a new request. Pass criterion: all recovery scenarios show `DISABLE` from the
initiating fault through acknowledgment and until a fresh request completes the
request-to-command pipeline.

CTX-01: The drone-control client is outside the system. It supplies enable, disable, and
recovery-acknowledgment events and receives the availability report. This contextual
role is inferred from the seed's drone-control equipment and battery-status flow.

CTX-02: The battery and power-status source is outside the system. It supplies the
qualitative battery observation and power-management evidence; the system neither
measures electrochemical state nor controls charging physics.

CTX-03: The engine and configuration evidence source is outside the system. It supplies
two engine-group snapshots and a structural configuration snapshot without asserting
their truth or any flight consequence.

CTX-04: The charging context source is outside the system. It reports whether the named
charger is disconnected, connected idle, charging, or unknown; charging control remains
external.

CTX-05: The power-and-propulsion actuation recipient is outside the system. It receives

switching and engine actuation are not modeled.
